name: browserai-payload
description: The vendored @playwright/mcp payload. Never published; this file exists only so the payload build has something to resolve.
//: THIS IS THE FLOAT, NOT A PIN. `latest` is the npm dist-tag, re-resolved from
an empty node_modules on every payload build. package-lock.json beside this
file records what it resolved to and is a provenance stamp, never a target:
build/Build-Payload.ps1 deletes the lock before installing, so nothing here
can hold a version back.
playwright-core is deliberately NOT declared as a DEPENDENCY here. It arrives
as @playwright/mcp's own exact dependency, and upstream publishes daily alphas:
on 2026-08-15 npm `latest` for playwright-core was 1.62.1 while the version
that actually ships was 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05. Declaring it would create a
second, independently floating source for a version upstream pins exactly.
THERE WAS AN `overrides` BLOCK HERE BETWEEN 2026-09-17 AND 2026-09-21, and it
is recorded rather than removed without trace. It pinned playwright-core to
1.64.0-alpha-2026-09-17 underneath @playwright/mcp 0.0.81, to pull
microsoft/playwright#42673 -- --file-paths=absolute, this project's own ask
#42497 -- one build forward of what the wrapper declared for itself. It was a
DATED EXCEPTION WITH A WRITTEN EXIT and the exit has fired: @playwright/mcp
0.0.82 declares playwright-core 1.64.0-alpha-1789764292000, whose own bundle
carries the fix. The wrapper's pin is what ships again, which is this file's
normal state and needs no entry of its own. See DECISIONS.md, 'The two
exceptions to the versioning policy', where the exception is recorded as
ENDED rather than deleted. NOTHING MAY BE ADDED BACK HERE ON THAT PRECEDENT:
the argument was a merged upstream fix one wrapper release had not caught up
with, which is a condition that expires, and it expired.
See CLAUDE.md, 'Versioning: everything floats, the build freezes it'.
